alerts.title: Low phosphate with TDF suggests tubular toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list renal failure and tubular wasting syndrome as TDF adverse effects, and recommend eGFR monitoring at 3, 6, then 6–12 monthly intervals, with closer monitoring in high-risk patients including those with co-existent hypertension. Patient has serum phosphate 0.78 mmol/L and trace proteinuria on TDF for 6 years with hypertension. TDF can cause proximal tubular dysfunction leading to phosphate wasting and proteinuria. Against drug attribution: trace proteinuria may stem from uncontrolled hypertension, and phosphate was measured only once without baseline comparison. However, the combination of low phosphate, proteinuria, and TDF exposure warrants evaluation for tubulopathy.

evidence.recommended_action: Check eGFR, urinary phosphate, and consider renal tubular function assessment. If tubulopathy confirmed, consider switching TDF to TAF or alternative NRTI.

alerts.title: TDF plus NSAID increases renal risk
alerts.message: Guidelines note TDF can cause renal failure and recommend eGFR monitoring, especially in high-risk patients with co-existent hypertension. Patient takes PRN ibuprofen alongside TDF and has hypertension with BP 146/94 and trace proteinuria today. Concurrent TDF and NSAID use compounds nephrotoxic risk through additive effects on renal tubular and haemodynamic function. The clinician's plan continues both TDF and PRN ibuprofen without flagging this interaction. Creatinine of 112 umol/L is within normal limits but represents a single snapshot; no trend data are available.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to minimise ibuprofen use; consider alternative analgesia. Monitor renal function more frequently given combined nephrotoxic risk.

alerts.title: eGFR not documented despite TDF risk factors
alerts.message: Guidelines require eGFR monitoring at 3 months, 6 months, then 6–12 monthly on TDF, with additional monitoring in high-risk patients including those with hypertension. Patient has been on TDF for 6 years and has hypertension, yet only serum creatinine is reported today without eGFR calculation. Trace proteinuria and low phosphate further elevate renal risk. The clinician's plan does not include eGFR assessment or enhanced renal monitoring. Creatinine alone may underestimate renal impairment, particularly in this higher-risk patient.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR from today's creatinine. Given hypertension and proteinuria, schedule renal monitoring at least every 6 months including eGFR and urinalysis.

alerts.title: EFV after 6 years: consider neuropsychiatric review
alerts.message: Guidelines list EFV as a current regimen component but do not explicitly address long-term EFV continuation thresholds. Patient has been on EFV for 6 years with viral suppression and CD4 of 540. He reports a heavy feeling in both thighs and stiff gait, which could reflect chronic EFV neuropsychiatric effects or peripheral neuropathy. Against drug attribution: symptoms are also consistent with occupational musculoskeletal strain from truck driving. No baseline neurological findings are documented for comparison. Many guidelines now prefer dolutegravir-based regimens over EFV for tolerability.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for EFV-related neuropsychiatric symptoms and peripheral neuropathy. Consider regimen review for potential switch to a better-tolerated ARV.

alerts.title: Trace proteinuria needs workup beyond hypertension
alerts.message: Guidelines identify TDF as a cause of tubular wasting syndrome and renal failure, and recommend enhanced monitoring in high-risk patients with hypertension. Patient has trace proteinuria attributed solely to hypertension in the plan, but TDF-related tubular dysfunction is an alternative or contributing cause, especially given low phosphate. The plan does not include quantitative protein assessment or renal tubular evaluation. Distinguishing hypertensive nephropathy from TDF tubulopathy requires further investigation, as management differs significantly.

evidence.recommended_action: Order urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and renal tubular markers. If TDF tubulopathy suspected, consider switching to TAF or alternative.
